extracted.intended_audience: BBC editorial staff, programme‑makers, independent production companies and content producers/journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational editorial standards describing how BBC output must treat audiences, contributors, sources and those featured, including principles of fairness, due care, consent, right of reply, and mandatory referral requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall fairness obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC strives to be fair to all – fair to its audiences, fair to its contributors and potential contributors, fair to sources and fair to those its output is about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general duty that applies across output and should be considered alongside related sections (eg Section 7 Privacy and Section 3 Accuracy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content based on respect, openness and straight dealing
rubrics_metrics.description: BBC content should be based on respect, openness and straight dealing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core editorial value that underpins decisions about recruitment of contributors, representations of people and interactions with sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unjust or unfair treatment (Ofcom compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC has an obligation under the Ofcom Broadcasting Code to 'avoid unjust or unfair treatment of individuals or organisations in programmes' (see Rule 7.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions must take account of Ofcom requirements as a baseline for fairness in broadcast output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due care to contributors, potential contributors and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Due care is owed to contributors or potential contributors, as well as to sources, who are at risk of harm or distress as a result of their contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due care is the level of care appropriate to the individual and particular circumstances; it includes assessing risks of harm or distress and adjusting editorial approach accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment factors for due care
rubrics_metrics.description: The assessment of due care takes into account the editorial content, the nature and degree of the individual's involvement and their public position, along with other relevant factors such as safety risks or whether the individual is vulnerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors should be weighed when deciding how to approach contributors (eg whether extra protections, anonymisation, or consent procedures are needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Material inaccuracies risk causing unfairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Material inaccuracies in the way people are referred to, or featured, may risk causing unfairness. This applies to scripted and unscripted content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When representing views or information about others (including portrayal of real people in drama), check accuracy and be mindful that inaccuracies can create unfairness; see Section 3: Accuracy for related requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent should normally be obtained
rubrics_metrics.description: The informed consent of contributors should normally be obtained. Individuals and organisations should be appropriately informed about the planned nature and context of their contributions before they participate unless there is an editorial justification for proceeding without their consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions require editorial justification (eg clear public interest) and should be documented; consider privacy implications per Section 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open, honest and straightforward dealings with exceptions (6.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC will be open, honest, straightforward and fair in its dealings with sources, contributors, potential contributors and audiences unless there is a clear public interest in doing otherwise, or unless there are important reasons such as legal matters, safety, or confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When considering deception, non-disclosure or restrictions on information, weigh public interest and legal/safety/confidentiality constraints; keep senior editorial oversight where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of reply for allegations or damaging critique (6.2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: When output contains allegations of wrongdoing, iniquity or incompetence or lays out a strong and damaging critique of an identifiable individual or organisation, those criticised should normally have a right of reply, unless there is an editorial justification to proceed without it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer an opportunity to reply in most cases; if refusing, record and justify the editorial reasons (eg public interest, legal concerns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of care when contribution may cause significant harm or distress (6.2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC owes a duty of care to its contributors or potential contributors, as well as to its sources, who may be at risk of significant harm or distress as a result of their contribution to the output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat potential for 'significant harm' as a trigger for heightened protections, referrals or editorial safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory referrals must be made in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory referrals must be referred in advance. Mandatory referrals are an essential part of the BBC's editorial and compliance process and must be observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a situation matches any listed mandatory referral, do not proceed without the required referral to senior editorial figures or Director Editorial Policy and Standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: serious allegation broadcast without offering reply (6.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to broadcast a serious allegation without offering an opportunity to reply must be referred to a senior editorial figure, or for independent production companies to the commissioning editor, and to Director Editorial Policy and Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not broadcast serious allegations without offering reply unless referral has occurred and approval recorded. (See 6.4.46.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: website concealing BBC connection (6.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to create a website which conceals any connection to the BBC must be referred to a senior editorial figure, or for independent production companies to the commissioning editor, and Director Editorial Policy and Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concealed BBC affiliation online raises transparency/fairness issues and requires high‑level sign‑off. (See 6.4.54.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: portrayal of a real person against wishes in drama (6.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The portrayal of a real person in a significant way in a drama against their wishes or those of their immediate surviving family must be referred to Director Editorial Policy and Standards for approval before a commitment is made to the production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek approval before committing to portrayals that could cause distress or unfairness to real people or their families. (See 6.4.58.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: entering a country to avoid visa restrictions (6.3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal for BBC content producers to enter a country in a way that avoids visa restrictions must be referred to a senior editorial figure, or for independent production companies to the commissioning editor. Director Editorial Policy and Standards must also be consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid circumventing legal/immigration rules for journalism/production without senior sign‑off. (See 6.4.57.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: paying more than a disturbance fee to contributors (6.3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals to pay anything more than a disturbance fee to contributors to news and current affairs output and factual journalism for telling their story must be referred to Editorial Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments above disturbance fee can compromise editorial integrity and must be cleared; see 6.4.13 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: proposed wording of appeals for contributors/contestants (6.3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed wording of all appeals for contributors and contestants, including those for talent and entertainment programmes, must be referred to a senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies, to the commissioning editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wording of appeals can influence participation and fairness; ensure senior review to prevent misleading or coercive language. (See 6.4.20.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: any access, filming or recording agreement (6.3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any access, filming or recording agreement must be referred to a senior editorial figure, or for independent production companies to the commissioning editor. Where the proposed wording risks compromising the BBC's editorial integrity or independence, Editorial Policy must also be consulted. If the wording cannot be amended to the BBC's satisfaction the production must not go ahead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts that constrain editorial independence require close scrutiny; refuse productions where satisfactory terms cannot be negotiated. (See 6.4.39.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: interviews/exclusive appearances by Royal Family (6.3.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request from output areas outside daily newsgathering for interviews with, or exclusive appearances by, members of the Royal Family must be discussed with the BBC's Royal Liaison Officer and Editorial Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Royal interviews require bespoke liaison and editorial oversight. (See 6.4.40.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: proposal to deceive a contributor in news/factual output (6.3.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to deceive a contributor to news or factual output must be referred to a senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies, to the commissioning editor. Editorial Policy must also be consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deception in journalism is a high‑risk tactic; obtain senior clearance and strong editorial justification. (See 6.4.50.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: proposal to deceive a contributor for comedy/entertainment/satire (6.3.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to deceive a contributor for comedy, entertainment or satirical purposes, whether or not they are in the public eye, must be referred to a senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies, to the commissioning editor. Editorial Policy must also be consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even entertainment deception requires referral and editorial oversight to assess fairness and potential harm. (See 6.4.53.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: proposal to create a false persona or social media account (6.3.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to create a false persona, or account on social media must be referred to a senior editorial figure, or for independent production companies to the commissioning editor. Editorial Policy must also be consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fabricated online identities by BBC staff/productions raise transparency and trust issues and need senior approval. (See 6.4.55.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral: covert intervention in online/social media discussions (6.3.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone actively intervening to steer the course of an online or social media discussion for a BBC purpose, without revealing their link to the BBC, must be acting in the public interest and must refer to a senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies, to the commissioning editor. Editorial Policy should also be consulted. In the most serious cases, referral must also be made to Director Editorial Policy and Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covert steering of online conversations requires strict justification and tiered referral depending on seriousness; record rationale and approvals. (See 6.4.56.)
